newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Oil Search says Kutubu is profit key.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Oil Search says Kutubu is profit key.

text.p: Papua New Guinea petroleum producer and explorer Oil Search Ltd said on Monday that its sharp rise in calendar 1996 earnings was due to higher oil production from the Kutubu fields, higher oil prices and cost control measures.

Chairman Trevor Kennedy said in a statement accompanying the profit result that the current year should bring greater value to shareholders as development work continued on the onshore Moran oil discovery permits and as the company sought commercial markets for its considerable gas reserves.
Kennedy said Moran, which stretches across three permit areas and had a 642 metre oil column from its highest to lowest point, was the most exciting discovery yet made in PNG.

"Experience in exploration in Papua New Guinea has taught us to expect surprises, however our present risk assessment of reserves in the Greater Moran area is in excess of those seen at Kutubu," he said. More drilling and appraisal work would be conducted on the region in 1997 to define the size of the field.
Chevron Corp is operator of the Moran field and has a 19.375 percent stake. Oil Search has a 7.763 percent holding.

Oil Search said 1996 net profit rose by 5.3 percent to A$24.05 million and earnings pre-tax and abnormals rose by 22.2 percent to A$48.0 million. Kennedy said short-term increases in oil production would come from the development of the Gobe-SE Gobe fields, with first production from the Gobe project expected sometime in the 1998 first quarter.
"Plateau production from Gobe and SE Gobe will average 50,0000 bpd, of which our share is around 12,000 bpd," he said.
"This will more than double our existing oil production from the Kutubu project in 1998."
Kennedy also said Oil Search would continue to consider acquisition of production-based assets or companies anywhere in the world to diversify its revenue base.
He said while Oil Search believed Discovery Petroleum Ltd fell into this category, it was fully priced by new owner London-based Premier Oil at 81 cents a share.

"Oil Search will continue to review production based opportunities, where they can be achieved at an appropriate price. Existing market circumstances indicate that acquisitions of this type are difficult to realise, based on this responsible criteria," Kennedy said.
Oil Search shares were five cents lower on Monday at A$2.60.
